content: Chloroquine phosphate belongs to a group of medications known as antimalarials and amebicides. It is prescribed to prevent and treat malaria, as well as to treat amebiasis. In some cases, it may be used for other medical conditions. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information if needed. This medication is available in tablet form and is taken orally. For adults using it to prevent malaria, a single dose is typically taken once a week on the same day each week. Your doctor will specify the number of tablets required per dose. The first dose should be taken two weeks before traveling to a malaria-endemic area, continued weekly while in the area, and for eight weeks after leaving the area. If starting two weeks in advance is not possible, your doctor may advise taking a double dose immediately. For treating acute malaria attacks in adults, an initial dose is taken immediately, followed by half the dose 6 to 8 hours later, and then half the dose once daily for the next two days. For infants and children, the dosage is determined based on their weight, and your doctor will calculate the appropriate amount. When treating amebiasis, the usual regimen involves taking one dose daily for two days, followed by half the dose daily for two to three weeks. This treatment is often combined with other amebicides. Chloroquine phosphate may cause stomach upset, so it is recommended to take it with food. Always follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Use the medication exactly as prescribed, and do not take more or less than directed. In addition to its primary uses, chloroquine phosphate is sometimes prescribed to alleviate symptoms of rheumatoid arthritis and to treat conditions such as systemic and discoid lupus erythematosus, scleroderma, pemphigus, lichen planus, polymyositis, sarcoidosis, and porphyria cutanea tarda. Discuss the potential risks of using this medication for these conditions with your doctor. Before starting chloroquine phosphate, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to this medication, chloroquine hydrochloride (Aralen HCl), hydroxychloroquine (Plaquenil), or any other drugs. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, supplements, and herbal products you are taking, especially acetaminophen, cimetidine, iron products, isoniazid, kaolin, magnesium trisilicate, methotrexate, niacin, rifampin, and vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have a history of liver disease, G-6-PD deficiency, hearing problems, porphyria or other blood disorders, psoriasis, vision changes, muscle weakness in your knees or ankles, or if you consume large amounts of alcohol. Additionally, inform your doctor if you have previously experienced vision changes while taking chloroquine phosphate, chloroquine hydrochloride, or hydroxychloroquine. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, let your doctor know, as this medication can harm a nursing infant. Unless otherwise instructed by your doctor, you may continue your normal diet while taking chloroquine phosphate. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Chloroquine phosphate may cause side effects. Minor side effects include headache, loss of appetite, diarrhea, upset stomach, stomach pain, skin rash or itching, hair loss, and mood or mental changes. If these symptoms persist or worsen, inform your doctor. Severe side effects require immediate medical attention and include visual disturbances (such as seeing light flashes, blurred vision, or difficulty reading), hearing problems, ringing in the ears, muscle weakness, drowsiness, vomiting, irregular heartbeats, convulsions, and difficulty breathing. If you experience any serious side effects, you or your doctor can report them to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store chloroquine phosphate in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from light, heat, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory, as regular monitoring is essential. Your doctor may order tests to evaluate your response to the medication and check for muscle weakness or vision changes. If you are on long-term chloroquine phosphate therapy, frequent eye exams are necessary due to the risk of serious vision problems. If you notice any changes in your vision, stop taking the medication and contact your doctor immediately. Do not share this medication with others, and consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription. Chloroquine phosphate is sold under the brand names Aralen® Hydrochloride and Aralen® Phosphate.
